topicName: Constructive Feedback and Code Review Etiquette
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Constructive Feedback and Code Review Etiquette"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Code reviews are a vital part of software engineering. They ensure code quality, share knowledge across the team, and maintain architectural consistency. However, poorly handled code reviews can damage team morale and create friction. Mastering the etiquette of giving and receiving constructive feedback is just as important as mastering syntax and algorithms."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"The Core Principles of Code Review Etiquette"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Review code, not the coder: Always separate the person from the code. Use objective language focused on the implementation rather than personal attributes."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Assume positive intent: Remember that your peers are trying their best. If a piece of code is confusing, assume there is context you are missing before reacting critically."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Explain the why: Never state that something is wrong without explaining the underlying reason, whether it is performance, security, readability, or maintainability."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Phrasing Feedback Constructively"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"The tone of your comments dictates how well they will be received. Small shifts in vocabulary can change a comment from hostile to collaborative."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"// Poor (Aggressive and subjective)\nWhy did you write this loop this way? It is completely inefficient."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"// Better (Objective and explanatory)\nHave we considered using a map operation here? It might improve performance with large datasets and makes the intent clearer."},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Categorizing Your Comments"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"To prevent overwhelming the author, clearly distinguish between critical blockers and minor suggestions by prefixing your comments appropriately."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"[Blocking]: Issues involving security vulnerabilities, breaking changes, or major logic flaws that must be fixed before merging."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"[Non-blocking]: Suggestions regarding naming conventions, stylistic preferences, or minor optimizations that the author can choose to adopt."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"[Question]: Inquiries for clarification where the intent of the code is not immediately obvious."},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for the Reviewee"},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Do not take feedback personally: Reviewers are targeting the code to help improve the final product and protect the codebase."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Be responsive and appreciative: Acknowledge comments quickly, even with a simple thumbs-up emoji, and thank reviewers for their time and attention to detail."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Discuss in person when stuck: If a thread exceeds three back-and-forth messages, move the conversation to a quick video call or huddle to resolve misunderstandings efficiently."}]
